title: Musk Reportedly Sought Intel, TSMC and Micron Plants Before Terafab Push
author: M
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Elon Musk reportedly explored buying semiconductor manufacturing facilities from Intel, TSMC and Micron before pursuing his ambitious Terafab project, according to The Elec. After those approaches were rejected, he shifted toward partnerships to support his expanding chipmaking ambitions.

The report says Terafab has contacted Korean suppliers and American equipment companies, including Lam Research and Applied Materials. Discussions reportedly cover piping, polishing slurries, cleaning chemicals and other materials essential to semiconductor production.

Suppliers have reportedly been surprised by the project’s execution speed, with engineers given authority to make decisions quickly. That approach could help accelerate development, although building and operating advanced semiconductor facilities remains a demanding technical undertaking.

Industry observers expect Terafab’s initial production target to reach 100,000 wafers per month before 2030. Musk’s eventual ambition is considerably larger: one million wafers monthly, supplying chips for autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots and other ventures.

Partnership discussions have also highlighted potential differences over operational control. Musk has said TSMC’s maximum involvement would be as a subcontractor. TSMC chief executive C.C. Wei, meanwhile, has indicated that his company would need to operate the plants for a partnership to work.

The supplied report also describes Intel as a Terafab partner, linking its involvement to its 14A manufacturing technology.

Beyond chip production, Musk connects these industrial plans to a broader vision of economic expansion beyond Earth. In a conversation with Walter Isaacson, he argued that physical artificial intelligence could conduct experiments, manufacture goods and enable activity in space.

Musk suggested that robots, lunar infrastructure and space development could eventually support an economy a million times larger than Earth’s.

For now, that remains an extraordinary long-term aspiration. Terafab’s immediate challenge is more concrete: converting supplier discussions, manufacturing partnerships and ambitious production targets into a functioning semiconductor operation capable of delivering chips reliably at the scale Musk ultimately envisions.

The Elec report — cited for Musk’s attempted plant purchases, supplier discussions and Terafab’s execution speed. I couldn’t independently access this page.
Walter Isaacson podcast on Apple Podcasts — supplied as the source for Musk’s remarks about AI, robots and a space economy.
